purpose: Repaint the older my own religion films reused in wave 1 (month one) so no two look the same (owner: "We can't have the same look for every film... You don't go to AMC and watch a movie that looks like the last one").
rules: no two my own religion month-one films within 3 days of each other share a look (new or reused); neighbouring days never match
each shot keeps its story beat and framing from the existing art; only the look changes (the old still is uploaded to ChatGPT as the layout reference)
no text in images unless the look needs it; vertical 9:16; no rainbow gradients
today shots get a diverse modern cast
today scenes: modern everyday people, diverse
no face of Jesus or of prophets such as Elijah: from behind, silhouette, hands or light
neighbours: new month-one my own religion films: 2 editorial, 24 comic, 29 fresco, 30 cutout.

films.suffix: Japanese sumi-e ink painting, huge confident single-breath black brushstrokes, splashed ink, wide white space, one hot vermilion accent, graphic and striking, no characters or seals with writing
films.why: a Chinese farmer's horse: bold ink brush
films.todayCast: a Black British woman in her twenties in London

shots.name: SW1-Frontier-Farm
shots.beat: Over two thousand years ago, a Chinese book called the Huainanzi told of an old man who lived near the northern frontier, with his son and their horses.

shots.name: SW2-Horse-Gone
shots.beat: One day his horse ran off across the border. The neighbors came to comfort him. What bad luck!

shots.name: SW3-Horses-Return
shots.beat: Months later, the horse came home, bringing fine horses from beyond the border. What good luck! the neighbors said. Who knows, said the old man, this could be bad luck.

shots.name: SW4-The-Fall
shots.beat: His son loved riding the new horses. He fell, and broke his leg, and was left with a limp. What bad luck! Who knows, said the old man.

shots.name: SW5-Officers-Come
shots.beat: A year later, raiders invaded. The young men took up bows to fight, and nine in ten frontier men died. The son, with his limp, stayed home.

shots.name: SW6-Today
shots.beat: Today, people retell it as the farmer who only ever says “maybe.” It’s an old answer to “everything happens for a reason.”
shots.cast: a Black British woman in her twenties in London

films.suffix: grainy 35mm film still, Kodak Portra 400 colour, natural light, visible grain and slight halation, candid documentary framing, real-looking people, push the grain and halation, hard real light, cinematic movie-still energy
films.why: Marcus Aurelius on campaign: 35mm movie still
films.todayCast: a Japanese man in his fifties in Tokyo

shots.name: MA1-Frontier-Camp
shots.beat: About eighteen centuries ago, Marcus Aurelius ruled Rome. He spent many of his last years in cold army camps on the far frontier, by the Danube river.

shots.name: MA2-The-Notebook
shots.beat: At night, by lamplight, he wrote notes to himself, in Greek. Not speeches. Reminders. Their old title is simply “To Himself.”

shots.name: MA3-Alexander
shots.beat: He reminded himself that he would die, like everyone. Alexander the Great and his mule driver, he wrote, ended up in the same place.

shots.name: MA4-Be-Good
shots.beat: He wrote: “Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over thee. While thou livest, while it is in thy power, be good.”

shots.name: MA5-The-Copy
shots.beat: His notes survived him, copied by hand for centuries. Today we call them the Meditations, and people still read them.

shots.name: MA6-Today
shots.beat: Today, a skull, an hourglass, two Latin words: memento mori, “remember that you will die.” It’s the same idea, and it’s really about today.
shots.cast: a Japanese man in his fifties in Tokyo

films.suffix: Kerala temple mural painting, ochre, red and green palette, bold black outlines, ornate crowns and jewellery, flat decorative space, intense ochre, red and green, bold black outlines
films.why: Shankara at Varanasi (he came from Kerala): Kerala mural
films.todayCast: a Brazilian woman and her older Haitian neighbour

shots.name: NB1-Ghats-Dawn
shots.beat: Long ago in Varanasi, at dawn, the young Hindu teacher Shankara walked down to bathe in the holy river Ganga, his students behind him.

shots.name: NB2-The-Stranger
shots.beat: A man came toward them with four dogs. The harsh caste rules of that time pushed his people to the edges, and told others not to touch them.

shots.name: NB3-Move-Aside
shots.beat: Move aside, Shankara told him. Get out of the way.

shots.name: NB4-The-Question
shots.beat: Move what? he asked. My body from yours, or the self in me from the self in you? The sun shines the same in the Ganga and my clay pot.

shots.name: NB5-The-Bow
shots.beat: Shankara bowed low before the man. Whoever truly sees this, he said, outcaste or priest, is my teacher. In many tellings, the man was the god Shiva.

shots.name: NB6-Today
shots.beat: Today, across India and Nepal, palms together and namaste is how people greet an aunt, a neighbor, a guest at the door.
shots.cast: a Brazilian woman and her older Haitian neighbour

films.suffix: claymation-look stop-motion set, handmade plasticine figures with visible fingerprints, miniature practical props, soft studio light, shallow depth of field, bright saturated plasticine colours, playful
films.why: Aesop's stuck ox cart: claymation comedy
films.todayCast: a white Irish woman in her forties

shots.name: AW1-Country-Road
shots.beat: An old Greek fable, told under the name of Aesop: a farmer was driving his ox cart home along a country road after the rain.

shots.name: AW2-Stuck-Wheel
shots.beat: The wheel sank deep into a muddy ditch. The oxen strained. The cart would not move.

shots.name: AW3-The-Wish
shots.beat: He stood by the road, hands idle, and begged Hercules, the mighty hero-god he honored most, to come and lift the cart for him.

shots.name: AW4-The-Answer
shots.beat: Hercules came, and said: take hold of the wheel, and drive your oxen. Call on the gods when you are working, or you call in vain.

shots.name: AW5-Free
shots.beat: So he put his shoulder to the wheel, the oxen pulled, and the cart rolled free.

shots.name: AW6-Today
shots.beat: Today, the vision board. “Manifesting” grew from an American movement of the 1800s. Research finds the dream works better with a look at the mud.
shots.cast: a white Irish woman in her forties

films.suffix: neon night photography, wet streets, magenta, lime and electric-blue glow from unreadable signs, long-exposure light trails, cinematic grain, neon-noir: lit like a neon night photo, magenta and electric-blue glow, deep black shadows, lime rim light
films.why: Jung's giant in the fog: neon-noir
films.todayCast: a Korean-American woman in her thirties

shots.name: JS1-Young-Jung
shots.beat: In Switzerland, a young man named Carl Jung, who would become a famous psychiatrist, had a dream he never forgot.

shots.name: JS2-Fog-Wind
shots.beat: It was night. He was pushing against a mighty wind through thick fog, his hands cupped around a tiny light that might go out at any moment.

shots.name: JS3-Giant-Behind
shots.beat: He looked back and saw a gigantic black figure following him. Afraid, he kept walking, still protecting the little light.

shots.name: JS4-Waking
shots.beat: When he woke, he understood. The giant was his own shadow, thrown onto the fog by the little light he carried.

shots.name: JS5-The-Word
shots.beat: Years later, Jung used the word shadow for the parts of ourselves we’d rather not claim. Not only dark ones. Hidden gifts, too.

shots.name: JS6-Today
shots.beat: Today, it’s called shadow work. Minus the jargon, it’s one question when someone bugs you more than they should: is any of this mine?
shots.cast: a Korean-American woman in her thirties

films.suffix: traditional Indian miniature painting in the Pahari and Rajput manner, fine brushwork, flat tilted perspective, jewel pigments, ornamental border with no writing, jewel-bright pigments, gold details
films.why: an Upanishad court scene: Indian miniature
films.todayCast: a Nigerian man and a Mexican-American woman in a busy office

shots.name: KM1-Janaka-Court
shots.beat: In the Upanishads, ancient Hindu teachings, King Janaka once offered a thousand cows, gold tied to their horns, to the wisest teacher in his court.

shots.name: KM2-Yajnavalkya
shots.beat: The sage Yajnavalkya calmly told his student to lead the cows home. The other scholars were not pleased. One by one, they stood up to question him.

shots.name: KM3-The-Question
shots.beat: Artabhaga asked the biggest question of all: when a person dies, and their breath and sight and speech return to nature, what becomes of that person?

shots.name: KM4-Aside
shots.beat: Take my hand, my friend, said Yajnavalkya. This is not for a crowd. Only the two of us should know. And they walked away together.

shots.name: KM5-What-They-Said
shots.beat: What did they talk about? Action. Karma. What they praised was action: a person becomes good by good action, and bad by bad action.

shots.name: KM6-Today
shots.beat: Today, “instant karma” means someone else getting what’s coming. The old word turns you around: what am I becoming, with this choice?
shots.cast: a Nigerian man and a Mexican-American woman in a busy office

films.suffix: Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Hokusai and Hiroshige, bold black outlines, flat Prussian blue, vermilion and pale green, dramatic sky gradients, crisp graphic waves and clouds, no writing or seals with characters
films.why: two Zen monks and a muddy road: ukiyo-e
films.todayCast: a young Arab-American man

shots.name: MR1-Muddy-Road
shots.beat: Long ago in Japan, two Zen monks, Tanzan and Ekido, were walking down a country road. The rain had turned it to mud.

shots.name: MR2-The-Crossing
shots.beat: At a bend they met a young woman in a silk kimono and sash. She couldn’t cross the mud without ruining it.

shots.name: MR3-Carried-Across
shots.beat: “Come on,” said Tanzan. He lifted her in his arms, carried her over the mud, and set her down on the other side.

shots.name: MR4-Silent-Walk
shots.beat: Then the monks walked on. Ekido said nothing, all afternoon. But inside, he was turning it over, and over, and over.

shots.name: MR5-Temple-Night
shots.beat: That night, at a temple, it burst out of him. “Monks don’t go near women! Especially young, lovely ones. Why did you do that?”

shots.name: MR6-Today
shots.beat: A sharp comment at nine in the morning can still be riding with you at midnight. Thoughts arrive. You don’t have to carry them.
shots.cast: a young Arab-American man

films.suffix: Tibetan thangka painting, mineral pigments on cotton, fine gold linework, deep lapis blue, vermilion and malachite green, ornate swirling clouds and lotus details, sacred balanced composition, saturated and jewel-bright
films.why: the Buddha touches the earth: thangka
films.todayCast: a Black American man in his sixties

shots.name: ET1-Bodhi-Tree
shots.beat: In Buddhist tradition, on the night of his awakening, Siddhartha sat beneath a great fig tree. He vowed not to rise until he understood.

shots.name: ET2-Mara-Comes
shots.beat: Then came Mara, the tempter, with storms and a shadowy army, trying to drive him from his seat. Siddhartha did not move.

shots.name: ET3-Who-Will-Speak
shots.beat: So Mara tried words. “This seat is mine. My army will speak for me. Who will speak for you?” Siddhartha was alone.

shots.name: ET4-Touching-Earth
shots.beat: He didn’t argue. He let his right hand slip down over his knee, and touched the earth with his fingertips.

shots.name: ET5-Dawn
shots.beat: By dawn the storm was gone, and Siddhartha had woken up. From then on he was called the Buddha, the one who is awake.

shots.name: ET6-Today
shots.beat: Today that hand reaches down in temples and homes all over the world. And your own feet are on the earth too, right now.
shots.cast: a Black American man in his sixties

films.suffix: Y2K chrome render, liquid-metal surfaces, iridescent highlights, glossy 3D bubble shapes, silver and lime reflections, glossy, futuristic, silver and lime reflections everywhere
films.why: Pascal's machine and the quiet room: Y2K chrome
films.todayCast: a mixed waiting room in Chicago: a Black teen, a white grandfather, a Latina mom, a South Asian man

shots.name: PQ1-Calculator
shots.beat: In France in the 1640s, a young man named Blaise Pascal built one of the first calculating machines, to help his father with tax sums.

shots.name: PQ2-Dice-Table
shots.beat: Later, a gambler’s question about dice led him to help work out the mathematics of chance. And he watched his friends.

shots.name: PQ3-The-Hunt
shots.beat: They gambled, they hunted, they rushed about at court. Take the hunter, said Pascal. He gallops all day after a hare.

shots.name: PQ4-Offered-Hare
shots.beat: But hand him the same hare as a gift, and he wouldn’t take it. It was never about the hare.

shots.name: PQ5-Quiet-Room
shots.beat: In an old translation of his notes: all the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber.

shots.name: PQ6-Today
shots.beat: Today the hare fits in a pocket. A waiting room, a red light, a quiet minute, and the hand goes. The chase, again.
shots.cast: a mixed waiting room in Chicago: a Black teen, a white grandfather, a Latina mom, a South Asian man

films.suffix: layered paper cut-out collage, cut and torn coloured paper, visible paper fibres and soft drop shadows, handmade diorama depth, bright saturated paper colours, lime, pink, saffron and cobalt
films.why: a Talmud story: Jewish papercut
films.todayCast: an Argentine family at dinner

shots.name: SS1-Emperor-Rabbi
shots.beat: This story is from the Talmud, the great book of Jewish teaching. A Roman emperor often talked with a Jewish sage, Rabbi Joshua.

shots.name: SS2-Shabbat-Table
shots.beat: In Jewish tradition, the Sabbath runs from Friday sundown to Saturday nightfall, a day of rest from work. The meal is cooked ahead.

shots.name: SS3-The-Question
shots.beat: One day the emperor asked him, “Why does your Sabbath food smell so wonderful?”

shots.name: SS4-Give-Me-Some
shots.beat: “Give me some!” said the emperor. He had the finest cooks in the empire.

shots.name: SS5-Only-If-You-Keep
shots.beat: “For one who keeps the Sabbath, it works,” said the rabbi. “For one who doesn’t keep it, it doesn’t.”

shots.name: SS6-Today
shots.beat: Today, for Sabbath-observant Jews, the phone is set down with the rest of the week’s work. Some others borrow the shape: one meal, phones away.
shots.cast: an Argentine family at dinner

films.suffix: single comic-book panel, bold inks, halftone shading, dynamic camera angles, strong flat colour, no speech bubbles, no lettering, graphic-novel inks, deep blacks, one hot accent colour
films.why: Elijah: wind, quake, fire, then a whisper: graphic-novel (prophet's face hidden)
films.todayCast: a Cree woman from Canada

shots.name: EL1-Desert-Flight
shots.beat: In the Hebrew Bible, the prophet Elijah was worn out and afraid. A powerful queen had threatened his life, so he ran far into the desert.

shots.name: EL2-Broom-Tree
shots.beat: Under a lone desert tree he lay down, ready to give up. An angel woke him with bread and water, and he walked on.

shots.name: EL3-The-Cave
shots.beat: He walked forty days to a holy mountain and slept in a cave. There he was told: go out, and stand on the mountain.

shots.name: EL4-Wind-Quake-Fire
shots.beat: A great wind tore at the rocks, but God was not in the wind. Then an earthquake, then a fire. God was not in them.

shots.name: EL5-Still-Voice
shots.beat: And after the fire, in the old English wording, came “a still small voice.”

shots.name: EL6-Today
shots.beat: Today the car, the shower and the walk to the store all get filled with sound. A quiet minute can be a mountain of its own.
shots.cast: a Cree woman from Canada

films.suffix: loose watercolour and ink wash, bleeding pigment, confident black ink linework, generous white paper, bold saturated pigment blooms, strong black ink, vivid not pale
films.why: a Daoist hermit: ink and watercolour
films.todayCast: a Filipino nurse in her twenties

shots.name: XY1-Yao-Travels
shots.beat: In an old Daoist story, Yao, a wise emperor of legend, went looking for a hermit named Xu You, who lived simply by a river.

shots.name: XY2-The-Offer
shots.beat: “When the sun and moon are out, why keep the torches burning?” said Yao. “You are the sun. Please, take my empire.”

shots.name: XY3-Tailorbird
shots.beat: “The tailorbird builds its nest in the deep forest,” said Xu You, “but it uses no more than one branch.”

shots.name: XY4-Mole-River
shots.beat: “The mole drinks from the river, but takes no more than a bellyful. Go home, my lord. I have no use for the empire.”

shots.name: XY5-Washing-Ears
shots.beat: In a later telling, Xu You was so unmoved by the offer that he went down to the river and washed out his ears.

shots.name: XY6-Today
shots.beat: Today the forest fits in a shopping cart. The glow of the new thing fades, and the wanting walks on. Xu You stopped at one branch.
shots.cast: a Filipino nurse in her twenties

films.suffix: stained-glass window art, jewel-toned glass panes with dark lead lines, sunbeams throwing coloured light across stone, stained-glass pop: saturated jewel colours, thick black leading, light blasting through
films.why: ten men healed, one comes back: stained-glass pop (no face of Jesus)
films.todayCast: a Black Brazilian grandmother and her family

shots.name: TL1-Village-Edge
shots.beat: In Luke’s Gospel, Jesus came to a village. Ten men with leprosy stood far off and called out: “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

shots.name: TL2-Go-Show
shots.beat: He told them: go, show yourselves to the priests. A priest could declare them clean, and let them come home.

shots.name: TL3-Healed
shots.beat: And as they went, they were healed.

shots.name: TL4-Turns-Back
shots.beat: One of them, seeing he was healed, turned back, praising God at the top of his voice.

shots.name: TL5-At-His-Feet
shots.beat: He fell at Jesus’s feet and thanked him. He was a Samaritan, from a people many Jews of his day kept apart from.

shots.name: TL6-Today
shots.beat: Today: the family dinner where everyone names one thing they’re thankful for. Half the table groans. It still counts. Out loud counts.
shots.cast: a Black Brazilian grandmother and her family

films.suffix: two- or three-colour risograph poster print, bold flat shapes, slightly misregistered ink, halftone dots, lime and black with one accent colour, lime, black and hot pink, big flat shapes, punchy
films.why: Confucius and one word: risograph poster
films.todayCast: a Chinese woman in her thirties on a Shanghai bus

shots.name: ZGO1-Courtyard
shots.beat: In ancient China, about 2,500 years ago, the teacher Confucius gathered students. One of the cleverest was named Zigong.

shots.name: ZGO2-The-Merchant
shots.beat: Zigong was quick, smooth-talking and very good with money. He did well as a merchant, and was sent out as a diplomat.

shots.name: ZGO3-Not-Yet
shots.beat: One day Zigong told his teacher: “What I don’t want others to do to me, I don’t want to do to them either.”

shots.name: ZGO4-One-Word
shots.beat: Another day, Zigong asked: “Is there one word you could live by for your whole life?”

shots.name: ZGO5-Like-Heart
shots.beat: Confucius said: “Is not reciprocity such a word? What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.”

shots.name: ZGO6-Today
shots.beat: Today: a sharp reply typed fast, thumb over send. Would I want this sent to me? One word for a whole life, one message at a time.
shots.cast: a Chinese woman in her thirties on a Shanghai bus

films.suffix: Kalighat pat painting, sweeping confident brush outlines, flat watercolour fills, bold curves, Bengali folk flair, bold saturated colour, big sweeping black brush lines
films.why: a king and queen talk at night: Kalighat
films.todayCast: a Turkish woman in her forties

shots.name: MLK1-Palace-Terrace
shots.beat: In the Buddha’s time, King Pasenadi and Queen Mallika sat together one evening on the palace terrace.

shots.name: MLK2-The-Question
shots.beat: The king asked her: “Mallika, is there anyone dearer to you than yourself?”

shots.name: MLK3-Her-Answer
shots.beat: “No, great king,” she said. “No one is dearer to me than myself. And you?” He thought, and said: “No, Mallika. Not for me either.”

shots.name: MLK4-To-The-Buddha
shots.beat: The king went to the Buddha and told him what they had said.

shots.name: MLK5-All-Directions
shots.beat: The Buddha said: search every direction with your mind, and you’ll find no one dearer to anyone than themselves.

shots.name: MLK6-Today
shots.beat: Today: the voice in the mirror after a long day. The Buddha’s reasoning starts right there. You’re dear to you. So is everyone else.
shots.cast: a Turkish woman in her forties

films.suffix: Gond tribal painting from central India, figures and animals filled with fine dot-and-dash line patterns, bold flat colours on a dark ground, hot orange, turquoise, lime and magenta, joyful and graphic
films.why: the half-golden mongoose: Gond animal art
films.todayCast: a Ghanaian man in his thirties

shots.name: MGS1-Great-Sacrifice
shots.beat: In the Mahabharata, after a great war, King Yudhishthira held a huge royal sacrifice. He gave away mountains of gold, grain and cows.

shots.name: MGS2-Golden-Mongoose
shots.beat: Then a mongoose appeared, half its body shining gold. It announced: this whole sacrifice is worth less than one little gift of barley flour.

shots.name: MGS3-Poor-Family
shots.beat: Once, the mongoose said, in a famine, a poor family of four gathered just enough barley flour for one small meal, and shared it four ways.

shots.name: MGS4-The-Guest
shots.beat: Before they ate, a hungry guest came to the door. The old man gave him his share. Still hungry. His wife gave hers. Then their son, then his wife.

shots.name: MGS5-Last-Share
shots.beat: The guest was Dharma, goodness itself, in disguise, and he blessed them. The mongoose rolled in their spilled flour, and half its body turned gold.

shots.name: MGS6-Today
shots.beat: Today: a bag of rice left in a street pantry box at dusk. No one watching. That’s the kind of gift the mongoose is still looking for.
shots.cast: a Ghanaian man in his thirties

films.suffix: woodblock print, carved line texture, limited flat colours, visible wood grain in the ink, strong silhouettes, bold two- and three-colour carving, strong black silhouettes, one hot red accent
films.why: Gethsemane at night: carved woodblock silhouettes
films.todayCast: a white American woman in her seventies

shots.name: GTH1-Into-The-Night
shots.beat: In Matthew’s Gospel, on the night before he died, Jesus ate a last supper with his friends, then walked out with them into the dark.

shots.name: GTH2-Olive-Garden
shots.beat: They came to an olive garden called Gethsemane. He took three close friends, Peter, James and John, a little further in.

shots.name: GTH3-Alone-Praying
shots.beat: He went a little further, fell on his face, and prayed, alone.

shots.name: GTH4-Asleep
shots.beat: He came back, and found them asleep.

shots.name: GTH5-Could-You-Not
shots.beat: “Could you not watch with me one hour?” he said to Peter. Then, gently: “The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

shots.name: GTH6-Today
shots.beat: Today: 2 a.m., the whole building asleep. You’re not the only one awake with something heavy. Not even close.
shots.cast: a white American woman in her seventies

films.suffix: hand-painted anime cel, clean ink lines, lush painted backgrounds like a 1990s theatrical anime feature, cinematic light and big skies, vivid saturated colour, dramatic light rays, epic scale
films.why: the universe in a toddler's mouth: anime cosmos
films.todayCast: a Vietnamese-American father and his toddler

shots.name: YSD1-Gokul-Yard
shots.beat: In Hindu tradition, Krishna is God come to earth. As a toddler in a village of cowherds, he was a handful. One day the boys saw him eating dirt.

shots.name: YSD2-Tattling
shots.beat: His big brother Balarama and the other boys ran to his mother, Yashoda: “Krishna ate mud!”

shots.name: YSD3-Open-Up
shots.beat: Yashoda took his little hand. Krishna looked up, all innocence. “I didn’t! They’re fibbing. Look in my mouth if you don’t believe me.”

shots.name: YSD4-The-Universe
shots.beat: She looked, and saw everything: sky and stars, mountains and oceans, fire, wind, the moon. And inside it all, her own village, and herself.

shots.name: YSD5-Mother-Again
shots.beat: She lifted him onto her lap and held him close. Just her little boy again, in the middle of everything.

shots.name: YSD6-Today
shots.beat: Today: a night sky far from the city, so full of stars it looks fake. For a moment you get small, in the good way.
shots.cast: a Vietnamese-American father and his toddler

films.suffix: Roman wall fresco, Pompeian red and ochre plaster, fine cracks in the surface, classical figures, soft faded pigment, bold Pompeian red and black panels, strong ochre and teal, crisp figures, not faded beige
films.why: Damon and Phintias in Syracuse: bold Greek-Roman wall painting
films.todayCast: two friends: an Ethiopian woman and a Polish woman

shots.name: DPH1-Syracuse
shots.beat: In ancient Syracuse lived two friends, Damon and Phintias. They were Pythagoreans, followers of the old teacher Pythagoras. Their saying: friends have all things in common.

shots.name: DPH2-The-Tyrant
shots.beat: The ruler, Dionysius, didn’t believe friendship like that was real. His courtiers said: let’s test it.

shots.name: DPH3-Condemned
shots.beat: So Phintias was accused of plotting and sentenced to die. He asked for the rest of the day to put his affairs in order.

shots.name: DPH4-Waiting
shots.beat: Damon stepped forward: if Phintias didn’t return, Damon would die in his place. The court laughed. Who comes back to die?

shots.name: DPH5-Sunset-Return
shots.beat: The sun sank lower. And just before it set, Phintias came back.

shots.name: DPH6-Today
shots.beat: Today: two old friends on a park bench at sunset, a small quarrel mended before dark. The kind of friend who comes back.
shots.cast: two friends: an Ethiopian woman and a Polish woman

films.suffix: Persian miniature painting in the Safavid manner, jewel-bright lapis, turquoise, coral and gold, fine detailed patterns on tiles, carpets and gardens, flat tilted perspective, ornamental border with no writing
films.why: Rumi in Konya: Persian miniature
films.todayCast: a young Mexican couple

shots.name: RMI1-Konya
shots.beat: In 1244, in the city of Konya, in today’s Turkey, Rumi was a respected Muslim scholar and teacher, with books, students and a fine name.

shots.name: RMI2-The-Pool
shots.beat: Then a wandering stranger came to town: Shams of Tabriz. In one popular telling, he found Rumi reading beside a pool.

shots.name: RMI3-Books-In-Water
shots.beat: Shams tossed the books into the water. Rumi cried out. Shams lifted them out, dry. “What is this?” Rumi asked. “Something you don’t know yet.”

shots.name: RMI4-Friends
shots.beat: The two became inseparable. Rumi’s students grew jealous. Then one day Shams was gone, and no one knows for sure what happened.

shots.name: RMI5-The-Reed
shots.beat: Out of the loss came an ocean of poems. His great work, the Masnavi, begins with a reed flute, crying.

shots.name: RMI6-Today
shots.beat: Today his name is on poems shared on phones every day, often with his faith left out. He was a Muslim scholar, and his poems are full of the Qur’an.
shots.cast: a young Mexican couple

films.suffix: claymation-look stop-motion set, handmade plasticine figures with visible fingerprints, miniature practical props, soft studio light, shallow depth of field, bright saturated plasticine colours, playful
films.why: an emperor who won't get up: claymation comedy
films.todayCast: a Black British woman in her fifties

shots.name: MBL1-Cold-Tent
shots.beat: Remember Marcus Aurelius, the emperor with the notebook? One cold morning, he lay under his blankets, and did not want to get up.

shots.name: MBL2-The-Argument
shots.beat: So he argued with himself, in writing. When you rise unwillingly, he told himself, remember: “I am rising to the work of a human being.”

shots.name: MBL3-Little-Workers
shots.beat: He looked at the little plants, the birds, the ants, the spiders, the bees, all busy doing their part to keep the world in order.

shots.name: MBL4-Feet-On-Floor
shots.beat: And you, a human being, he asked himself, won’t do a human’s work?

shots.name: MBL5-The-Work
shots.beat: For a Stoic, a human’s work was simple to say: be kind, be fair, be useful to the people around you.

shots.name: MBL6-Today
shots.beat: Today: the alarm, the warm covers, the bargaining. Get up, not to be impressive, but because there’s a human’s work waiting.
shots.cast: a Black British woman in her fifties

films.suffix: 1960s pop-art print, big Ben-Day dots, thick black outlines, flat punchy red, yellow, cyan and hot pink, graphic close-up framing, maximal contrast
films.why: Epictetus and a cruel master: pop-art (no harm shown)
films.todayCast: an older white veteran with a cane in Ohio

shots.name: EPL1-Roman-House
shots.beat: In the Roman Empire, almost two thousand years ago, a boy from what’s now Turkey grew up enslaved. His name, Epictetus, means “acquired.” Bought.

shots.name: EPL2-The-Master
shots.beat: An old story says his master once began twisting his leg. Epictetus looked up and said, quietly: “You will break it.”

shots.name: EPL3-Calm-Face
shots.beat: The master kept twisting, and the leg broke. Epictetus said, calmly: “Didn’t I tell you that you would break it?”

shots.name: EPL4-The-Staff
shots.beat: To be honest about it: this story comes from one Roman writer, Celsus. Another old source says illness made him lame. No one knows for sure.

shots.name: EPL5-Teaching
shots.beat: What is known: Epictetus was lame, was freed, and became a famous teacher. He taught: “Lameness is an impediment to the leg, but not to the will.”

shots.name: EPL6-Today
shots.beat: Today: a bad knee, a hard diagnosis, a person who won’t change. Some things aren’t yours to fix. The voice you answer in still is.
shots.cast: an older white veteran with a cane in Ohio

films.suffix: Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Hokusai and Hiroshige, bold black outlines, flat Prussian blue, vermilion and pale green, dramatic sky gradients, crisp graphic waves and clouds, no writing or seals with characters
films.why: Zeno's shipwreck: ukiyo-e great wave
films.todayCast: a young Somali-American man

shots.name: ZNS1-Purple-Cargo
shots.beat: More than 2,300 years ago, a merchant named Zeno sailed from Phoenicia with a cargo of precious purple dye.

shots.name: ZNS2-The-Wreck
shots.beat: Near Athens, the ship was wrecked. The cargo, the fortune, all of it went into the sea.

shots.name: ZNS3-Ashore
shots.beat: Zeno made it ashore with almost nothing. He was about thirty, in a city where he knew no one.

shots.name: ZNS4-Bookshop
shots.beat: He wandered into a bookshop and sat down. The bookseller was reading aloud from a book about Socrates.

shots.name: ZNS5-Hooked
shots.beat: Zeno was hooked. Socrates questioned everything, owned almost nothing, and wasn’t afraid. Zeno had lost everything, and found his life’s work.

shots.name: ZNS6-Today
shots.beat: Today: the job that ended, a box of desk things, a bookshop window. Not every loss leads somewhere good. But a few pages can still change a life.
shots.cast: a young Somali-American man

films.suffix: 1990s music-video VHS still, chromatic aberration, scan lines, tape noise, saturated colour, handheld low-angle energy, hot magenta and cyan colour bleed, high energy
films.why: Zeno follows Crates through Athens: VHS street energy
films.todayCast: a young Korean man

shots.name: CRT1-Bookshop-Door
shots.beat: Zeno looked up from the book about Socrates and asked the bookseller: where can I find people like this, today?

shots.name: CRT2-Following
shots.beat: It was Crates, a Cynic philosopher. Born rich, he had given it all away, and said exactly what he thought. Zeno followed him.

shots.name: CRT3-Door-Opener
shots.beat: today, when a small embarrassment comes, a wrong name, a spill, a typo in the group chat, say crates’s line to yourself: nothing terrible has happened to you. then carry on.

shots.name: CRT4-Lentil-Pot
shots.beat: But Zeno was shy. So Crates handed him a pot of lentil soup and told him to carry it through a busy part of Athens.

shots.name: CRT5-The-Crack
shots.beat: Zeno hid it under his cloak. Crates cracked the pot with his staff. Soup ran down Zeno’s legs, and he ran.

shots.name: CRT6-Today
shots.beat: Today: coffee down your shirt on a full train. Everyone looks. Spilled soup is only spilled soup.
shots.cast: a young Korean man

films.suffix: high-fashion editorial photograph, styled wardrobe, sculptural studio or location light, medium-format crispness, magazine-cover composure, dark seamless backdrop or bold location, single hard spotlight, fashion-magazine drama
films.why: teaching on the painted porch: fashion-editorial light
films.todayCast: a Moroccan woman and an Indian man

shots.name: STA1-Agora
shots.beat: Zeno didn’t teach in a private school. He taught in a public place, where people passed all day: the edge of the marketplace in Athens.

shots.name: STA2-Under-Columns
shots.beat: He taught under a stoa, a long porch of columns. His was the painted porch, its walls covered in famous paintings of battles.

shots.name: STA3-The-Talker
shots.beat: Anyone could stop and listen, and anyone could talk. One day a young man wouldn’t stop talking, mostly nonsense.

shots.name: STA4-Two-Ears
shots.beat: Zeno said: “The reason we have two ears and only one mouth is that we may listen more and talk less.”

shots.name: STA5-Honored
shots.beat: Athens honored him for a life that matched his words. They even trusted him with the keys to the city walls.

shots.name: STA6-Today
shots.beat: Today: lunch in a busy plaza, a friend mid-story. Two ears, one mouth. Let them finish. Wisdom in the open.
shots.cast: a Moroccan woman and an Indian man

films.suffix: grainy 35mm film still, Kodak Portra 400 colour, natural light, visible grain and slight halation, candid documentary framing, real-looking people, push the grain and halation, hard real light, cinematic movie-still energy
films.why: Cleanthes hauling water at night: 35mm grit
films.todayCast: a young Kenyan man

shots.name: CLW1-Night-Well
shots.beat: Cleanthes was a boxer who came to Athens, the story goes, with almost no money. He wanted to study with Zeno at the painted porch.

shots.name: CLW2-At-The-Porch
shots.beat: When Zeno died, the one who took over the school wasn’t the quickest student. It was Cleanthes, the water carrier.

shots.name: CLW3-The-Council
shots.beat: Summoned to explain how he lived, he brought witnesses: the gardener whose water he drew, and a woman whose grain he ground.

shots.name: CLW4-The-Gift
shots.beat: The court was so impressed it voted him a gift of money. Zeno told him not to accept it.

shots.name: CLW5-Oyster-Shells
shots.beat: Other students called him the donkey. Fine, he said: then I’m the one strong enough to carry Zeno’s load. He wrote his notes on oyster shells.

shots.name: CLW6-Today
shots.beat: Today: the dishes at ten at night. One plate, then the next. Not beneath you. Carry the water.
shots.cast: a young Kenyan man
